problem.title: Manage what comes back
problem.intro: A sold item leaves the business. A rented item still has to come back — on time, in the right condition and ready for the next booking.
problem.flow: Booking → handover → in transit → return → inspection → available again

items.title: Prevent two bookings, one item
items.body: The same unit is promised to two customers for the same weekend because the return and inspection window did not block the next booking.

items.title: Settle deposits without guesswork
items.body: At return, someone has to decide what to refund, what to retain and how to explain the amount.

items.title: Find the current equipment status
items.body: It may be with the customer, with a courier, at a pickup point or waiting for inspection — but there is no single view of where it stands.

problem.closing: Avably is being designed around the full rental cycle, not only the booking.
problem.warehouseAlt: Rows of equipment prepared for upcoming rentals
problem.useAlt: Work equipment in use away from the warehouse

founder.title: Build with someone who rents
paragraphs: I run an equipment rental business. I know the weekend with two bookings against the same unit, the hunt for the deposit record and the question of whether an item is still with the customer, already in transit or waiting to be checked.

Avably comes from that day-to-day operational need. It is still at an early stage, so I do not want to guess how every rental business works. The first companies will help decide which workflows have to work first.
founder.signature: Maciej — founder of Avably and rental business owner
